items.heading: How EB-5 works
items.text: Each step between the investment and the green card, in order, and what the law requires of the business that receives the money.

image.alt: A building under construction with two cranes and its concrete frame exposed

items.heading: How much to invest
items.text: The minimum is $1,050,000 and drops to $800,000 in a targeted employment area (TEA), which means a rural area or one with high unemployment. You see what the inflation adjustment changes for petitions filed in 2027 or later.

image.alt: A white scale model of an apartment building with a pool on a wooden table, with a ruler, a pencil and a rolled drawing beside it

items.heading: Regional center or direct investment
items.text: A regional center is an entity approved by USCIS, the U.S. immigration agency, that pools several investors in the same project. You see how each path reaches the 10 jobs required per investor, all of them full time.

image.alt: A printed site plan on a wooden table, with a pen and a cup of coffee

items.heading: Source of funds
items.text: How to document where the invested money came from. The examples cover the sale of a home or a company in Brazil, an inheritance and a loan.

image.alt: A stack of light folders tied with a ribbon, with a fountain pen on top

items.heading: Risk and getting your capital back
items.text: Where your money sits in the project, what happens if construction runs late and what repayment of your capital depends on. Litora doesn't promise a return, and the webinar explains why.

image.alt: Concrete columns and slabs of a building under construction, with rebar showing

items.heading: Family, timing and taxes
items.text: Which family members are included, what the timing depends on and what the green card changes in the tax on your income from Brazil. You leave with the questions to take to your tax advisor.
